claim: Before interrogation the questioner must advise the three Article 31(b) rights: nature of the accusation, right to remain silent, statement may be used at court-martial
quote: informing the accused or suspect of the nature of the accusation; ... right to remain silent; ... any statement made may be used as evidence

claim: Right to consult counsel before answering questions and have counsel present attaches to every Article 31 interrogation (also lines 63-79, 140, 199)
quote: If a person suspected of an offense and subjected to custodial interrogation requests counsel, any statement ... is inadmissible unless counsel was present
fix: Say the counsel right under Mil. R. Evid. 305 attaches in custodial interrogation or after preferral of charges. Outside those, Article 31 gives silence and the three warnings only. Questioning stops on any invocation of silence. It stops until counsel is present only for custodial or post-preferral interrogation.

claim: Once you invoke counsel, all questioning must stop until counsel is present
quote: If a person chooses to exercise the privilege against self-incrimination, questioning must cease immediately.
fix: Split the rule. Silence invocation ends questioning. Counsel invocation ends questioning until counsel is present only under 305(c)(2) or (c)(3).

claim: Defense Counsel is free and a civilian attorney is at your expense
quote: a judge advocate ... will be provided by the United States at no expense ... the person may retain civilian counsel at no expense to the United States

claim: Article 31 applies when ALL THREE conditions are met (subject to UCMJ questioner, suspect, interrogation)
quote: a person subject to the code may not interrogate or request any statement from an accused or a person suspected of an offense
fix: Add that a request for a statement, not only interrogation, triggers the warnings.

claim: The U.S. Supreme Court extends Article 31 to civilian investigators acting under military direction
quote: This term includes, for purposes of subdivision (c) of this rule, a knowing agent of any such person or of a military unit.
fix: Cite Mil. R. Evid. 305(b)(1) knowing-agent language. Drop the Supreme Court attribution (also lines 287).

claim: Persons subject to the UCMJ listed as active duty, reservists on active duty, cadets and midshipmen, prisoners serving court-martial sentences
quote: No Article 2 text located in the archive set for this cluster. Reserve component members are also subject during inactive-duty training and the list omits retirees entitled to pay.
fix: List the Article 2 categories from the statute or cite Article 2 directly.

claim: Routine administrative questions (name, rank, unit, DoD ID) do not trigger Article 31
quote: any formal or informal questioning in which an incriminating response either is sought or is a reasonable consequence

claim: Custody is not required for Article 31 warnings
quote: Custodial interrogation ... is separately defined; Article 31 warnings under (c)(1) carry no custody element

claim: Article 31 protects testimonial evidence, not physical evidence (sobriety tests, DNA, fingerprints)
quote: The privileges against self-incrimination are applicable only to evidence of a testimonial or communicative nature.

claim: Statements obtained in violation of Article 31 are generally inadmissible (Mil. R. Evid. 304)
quote: A statement obtained in violation of this rule is involuntary and will be treated under Mil. R. Evid. 304.

claim: JAGMAN (5800.7G) governs command investigations, three types: command investigation, litigation-report, court of inquiry
quote: TYPE ONE: COMMAND INVESTIGATIONS ... TYPE TWO: LITIGATION-REPORT ... TYPE THREE: COURTS AND BOARDS OF INQUIRY
fix: Name Type Three as courts and boards of inquiry. Also cite the correct short title JAGINST 5800.7G.

claim: Command investigation is conducted by a command-appointed officer or SNCO
quote: Most command or litigation-report investigations will be conducted by a commissioned officer, but a warrant officer, senior enlisted person, or civilian employee may also be used
fix: Say commissioned officer in most cases. A warrant officer, senior enlisted Marine or civilian is the exception the convening authority approves.

claim: Court of Inquiry is highest-level and rarely convened
quote: should be reserved for the investigation of major incidents ... Convened by a GCMCA, or a person designated by the Secretary of the Navy

claim: Investigator must read Article 31 rights before continuing questioning once the witness becomes a suspect
quote: Before the interview, military personnel suspected of a criminal offense must be advised of Article 31, UCMJ, warnings

claim: As a witness you have a duty to provide truthful information and refusal may be Article 92 misconduct
quote: Military witnesses may be required to swear or affirm that their statement is truthful or to provide recorded testimony under oath.

claim: MCO 5800.16 Vol 11 (Administrative Separations and Investigations) supports Article 31 rights
quote: VOLUME 11 ADMINISTRATIVE SEPARATIONS AND INVESTIGATIONS
fix: Volume title is right. Article 31 rights text sits in JAGMAN Ch I and Mil. R. Evid. 305, not Vol 11. Cite those for the rights. Cite Vol 11 for separations.

claim: Reach Defense Counsel at the installation LSSS or OSJA (also lines 329, 333)
quote: The Legal Services Support Sections (LSSS) ... have been renamed Regional Law Centers (RLC) ... independent Defense Services Organization (DSO)
fix: Send Marines to the Defense Services Organization at the Law Center. LSSS is now Regional Law Center or Law Center. OSJA is not a Marine Corps term. Use SJA office for command legal advice.

claim: Coordinate with the unit S-1 to reach Defense Counsel
quote: DSO ... will now have their own supervisory chain
fix: Contact DSO directly. No paragraph routes defense requests through S-1.

claim: Lying to investigators is an Article 107 false official statement offense
fix: Statute not located in the cluster archive text. Substance is correct law. Cite Article 107 from the MCM Part IV.

claim: MCO 3040.4 is titled Marine Corps Casualty Procedures Manual (also line 17)
quote: REF B IS MCO 3040.4, THE MARINE CORPS CASUALTY ASSISTANCE PROGRAM
fix: Retitle as Marine Corps Casualty Assistance Program.

claim: MCO 3040.4 was cancelled by MARADMIN 186/25 (candidate from superseded list)
quote: this MARADMIN cancels reference (a) and further clarifies reporting requirements previously published in chapter 3 of reference (b)
fix: False positive. The message cancels MARADMIN 226/07, not MCO 3040.4. MCO 3040.4 stands. Add MARADMIN 186/25 for PCR reporting through the DCIPS-PCR spreadsheet.

claim: MCO 1770.1 (Casualty Assistance Calls Program) governs
fix: No MCO 1770.1 file resolves in the text cache. Add the document to the archive before the next verification.

claim: JAGMAN Part E Section 0212 paragraph B quote on LOD determination for active duty deaths
quote: A line of duty determination is required whenever an active duty service member of the Naval service dies

claim: JAGMAN Part E is titled Investigations
quote: PART E -- LINE OF DUTY/MISCONDUCT
fix: Part E is Line of Duty/Misconduct. Death-case investigation rules sit in Part F, 0225-0231. Chapter II is Administrative Investigations.

claim: Command investigations are required for every Marine death
quote: Each active duty death shall be subject to, at a minimum, a preliminary inquiry ... shall decide whether the preliminary inquiry is sufficient
fix: State the minimum is a preliminary inquiry. An investigation follows when the command or higher authority finds the inquiry insufficient.

claim: GCMCA makes the line of duty determination on the command investigation
quote: The GCMCA with an assigned judge advocate is the cognizant official for making the formal line of duty determination

claim: Command investigation is convened by the commanding officer, final action by the GCMCA
quote: forward the inquiry/investigation to the first GCMCA ... with an assigned judge advocate
fix: Add the written recommendation the command sends with the report.

claim: Investigation information flows to next of kin through the CACO until the redacted report is delivered
quote: upon completion of the review by the first GCMCA ... the reviewer shall release an advance copy of the investigation, upon a request, to the next of kin
fix: Add that an advance copy goes to the NOK on request once the first GCMCA finishes review.

claim: LODD for reservists: death during active duty, IDT, travel to or from training; not required for purely civilian status
quote: In many cases, the death of a reservist will also require a line of duty determination.

claim: In line of duty: full SBP eligibility. Out of line of duty: reduced or eliminated
quote: If the service member was not retirement eligible at the time of death, then SBP is inapplicable.
fix: Add the rule. A line of duty death pays 55 percent of 75 percent of base pay. A non-line-of-duty death pays only a retirement-eligible survivor, on retirement-for-service rules.

claim: Simple investigations complete in 30 to 60 days. Initial investigation convened within days
quote: shall not normally exceed 20 calendar days from the date of the death, or its discovery. For good cause, however, the CA may extend
fix: State the 20 calendar day completion standard and 20 days for the CA and reviewers to endorse. Extensions need reviewing authority coordination.

claim: Complex cases take 6 months to 2+ years; no required update cadence
quote: Investigating agencies will provide an update to the appropriate Military Service Casualty Headquarters office at a 30-day frequency until the investigation is completed.
fix: Add the 30-day status update to the casualty office.

claim: Investigation Tracking at HQMC tracks all command investigations and preliminary inquiries of Marine deaths
quote: Serve as the single activity responsible for tracking and archiving the executive summary and endorsements of all injury and death investigations.

claim: Investigation Tracking phone 800-847-1597
quote: Marine Corps Casualty Office at 800-847- 1597
fix: The number is the Marine Corps Casualty Office line (MFPC). Label it so.

claim: Email usmc-investigations@usmc.mil and LTAP numbers (866-210-3421)
fix: No archive file carries this email or the LTAP numbers. Verify against the live HQMC MFPC page.

claim: Naval Safety Center investigates aviation mishaps and ship mishaps
fix: No paragraph found assigning mishap investigation to the Naval Safety Center. Safety investigations are privileged and kept apart from JAGMAN reports (0207d(1)). Describe safety investigations as separate and not usable in the JAGMAN report.
